note: Source of truth for engines/governance/hardcode-decision-engine.ts classify(). Categories are mutually exclusive — every value found in source gets exactly one.
policy: ห้ามใช้กฎแบบห้ามฮาร์ดโค้ดทั้งหมดโดยไม่แยกบริบท — every value must be classified before a verdict is given. UNKNOWN is always blocked pending human review; the engine must never guess ALLOWED.

FORBIDDEN_HARDCODE.description: Value must never appear literally in source: secrets, IDs that vary per tenant/environment, prices/thresholds/business rules, workflow state, machine-dependent paths, environment-dependent domains.

REQUIRED_HARDCODE.description: Standard/fixed values that must live in source, but only inside a constants or protocol-definition module with full provenance metadata — never scattered across files.
REQUIRED_HARDCODE.must_not: duplicate the same constant across multiple files

PROTOCOL_CONSTANT.description: Value defined by an external protocol/standard the app must speak correctly (HTTP, MIME, OAuth path shape, etc). Safe to hardcode inside a protocol-definition module.

HARDWARE_CONSTANT.description: Value tied to a specific, unchanging hardware model — datasheet register map, fixed-board pin map, firmware-fixed opcode. If it varies by device model, it is NOT this category — see hardware-profile-registry.

PLATFORM_CONSTRAINT.description: Limit imposed by the OS/runtime/framework itself (e.g. max path length, framework-reserved config keys). May live in the framework's own config file, never mixed with business config.

COMPILE_TIME_CONSTANT.description: Language-level or enum constant resolved at compile time, no runtime variability possible.

CONFIGURABLE_VALUE.description: Varies by deploy/environment but is not secret. Belongs in a config file or env var, never inline.

REGISTRY_VALUE.description: Belongs in one of the DNA OS registry/*.json files (business rule, capability mapping, service metadata) — the existing registry pattern used throughout this repo.

ENVIRONMENT_SECRET.description: Any credential, key, token, or password. Always a SECURITY_VIOLATION if found literally in source.

BUSINESS_RULE.description: Pricing, thresholds, workflow logic specific to this business. Must come from Policy Engine or Database, never inline in route/UI/business logic.

RUNTIME_RESOLVED_VALUE.description: Value that can only be known at runtime (request context, current user, current session). Must never be hardcoded as a stand-in/default.

UNKNOWN.description: Engine cannot confidently classify. Always blocked pending human review — never presented as allowed.

MODULE_PATH.description: A relative or path-aliased module specifier used in an import/require-shaped position (e.g. './queries', '../lib/x', '@/engines/tax'). Structural to the module system, not a business or protocol value.
MODULE_PATH.allow_conditions: Value matches ^(\.\.?/|@/)[\w\-./]+$ (relative or @-aliased path shape), contains no whitespace, no '://' (not a URL), no query string.
MODULE_PATH.reject_conditions: Value starts with http(s):// (that's CONFIGURABLE_VALUE/service endpoint, not a module path). Value contains a space or Thai character (not a valid module specifier — likely misclassified). Value is used as a runtime file-system path built from user input (that's FORBIDDEN_HARDCODE, machine-specific path).
fail_examples: ไฟล์ต้นทาง
MODULE_PATH.registry_reference: n/a — validated by shape only (import specifiers aren't centrally registered in this codebase); deliberately narrow shape regex substitutes for a registry cross-reference here.
MODULE_PATH.why_not_business_rule_or_secret: A module import path carries no business meaning and is never a credential — it identifies which source file is loaded, resolved at build/bundle time by the module system, not read as configuration.

EVENT_NAME.description: A dot.case event-type string (e.g. 'hardcode.detected') that literally appears as a key in registry/events.json — the codebase's single real event-name registry.
EVENT_NAME.allow_conditions: Value matches ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*\.[a-z][a-z0-9_.]*$ AND the exact string is a real key in registry/events.json's `events` object.
EVENT_NAME.reject_conditions: Dot.case-shaped string that is NOT a registered event name (stays UNKNOWN, not guessed as an event just because it looks like one — shape alone is insufficient, verified in HCG-P1's own investigation).
fail_examples: debt.find (that's a COMMAND_NAME, not an event)
EVENT_NAME.registry_reference: registry/events.json (events object keys) — cross-referenced at classify() time, not guessed from shape.
EVENT_NAME.why_not_business_rule_or_secret: An event-type identifier names a structural occurrence in the system's own event registry; it carries no price/threshold/credential meaning and is meaningless without the already-registered schema behind it.

COMMAND_NAME.description: A dot.case command string (e.g. 'invoice.items') that literally appears as a key in registry/command-registry.json — the codebase's single real command registry (also the Command Dispatcher's own source of truth, engines/validation/dispatcher.ts).
COMMAND_NAME.allow_conditions: Value matches ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*\.[a-z][a-z0-9_.]*$ AND the exact string is a real key in registry/command-registry.json's `commands` object.
COMMAND_NAME.reject_conditions: Dot.case-shaped string not present in command-registry.json — the Command Dispatcher itself would reject it as a 'Shadow Command' (engines/validation/dispatcher.ts dispatch(), 'ไม่อยู่ใน registry — Shadow Command ถูกปฏิเสธ'), so an unregistered lookalike string is exactly the case that must stay UNKNOWN, not be waved through.
fail_examples: debt.delete (not a registered command as of this entry)
COMMAND_NAME.registry_reference: registry/command-registry.json (commands object keys) — the exact same source engines/validation/dispatcher.ts's isRegistered() checks against.
COMMAND_NAME.why_not_business_rule_or_secret: A command name selects which already-vetted, already-schema-defined operation runs; it is a structural dispatch key, not a price/threshold or a credential — and it is meaningless unless independently already registered, which is the whole point of the cross-reference.

SCHEMA_IDENTIFIER.description: A snake_case, underscore-containing literal (e.g. 'line_user_id', 'created_at') that matches a real table or column name extracted from supabase/migrations/*.sql.
SCHEMA_IDENTIFIER.allow_conditions: Value matches ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$, contains at least one underscore (deliberately excludes single dictionary words like 'amount'/'label'/'item'/'error'/'key' that coincidentally collide with a real column name elsewhere but are actually generic property names in this call site — checked live: 44 raw matches against the schema cache dropped to 6 once the underscore requirement was added, removing exactly the ambiguous single-word false-approval risk), AND the exact string is present in registry/hardcode-governance/schema-identifier-cache.json's tables[] or columns[] array.
SCHEMA_IDENTIFIER.reject_conditions: snake_case value NOT present in the schema cache (stays UNKNOWN). Value also matches a business-rule keyword (threshold/price/timeout/retry/ราคา) — that check runs earlier in classify() and wins, since a column NAME and a column's business-meaningful VALUE are different things (e.g. 'debt_threshold' the identifier vs. 5000 the value — this category only ever classifies the identifier-shaped literal, never a business number).
fail_examples: amount (ambiguous single word, not schema-specific enough)
debt_threshold (business rule identifier, not a schema reference — see BUSINESS_RULE)
SCHEMA_IDENTIFIER.registry_reference: registry/hardcode-governance/schema-identifier-cache.json, generated by scripts/hcg-build-schema-cache.ts from supabase/migrations/*.sql (102 files, 63 tables, 326 columns as of 2026-08-04) — regenerate after schema changes; this is a cache, not a live query.
SCHEMA_IDENTIFIER.why_not_business_rule_or_secret: A table/column name is structural database metadata (what a value is called), never the value itself, never a threshold/price, and never a credential.

UI_LITERAL.description: Human-readable display/message text — UI labels, log lines, error/status messages — identified by containing whitespace or Thai-script characters (a real, non-guessable structural signal: no machine identifier, business key, or credential is ever written with embedded spaces or Thai prose in this codebase's real conventions).
UI_LITERAL.allow_conditions: Value contains a space character OR a Thai-script character (U+0E00–U+0E7F), length >= 4, AND does not match any FORBIDDEN_HARDCODE/ENVIRONMENT_SECRET pattern (checked earlier in classify() and always wins), AND context_key does not match a security-sensitive keyword (key|token|secret|password|pwd|credential|รหัส|ผ่าน) — defensive check since forbidden-pattern keyword coverage is English-only today (see forbidden-hardcode-patterns.json) and a Thai-labeled secret must not slip through via this category.
UI_LITERAL.reject_conditions: Value matches a forbidden secret pattern (wins first, always). Value's context_key suggests a security-sensitive field even in Thai. Value contains '${' (template-literal interpolation) — that is not a pure literal at all, stays UNKNOWN/unclassified by this category (a separate, not-yet-solved gap, noted honestly in this phase's report).
pass_examples: preview_token ไม่ถูกต้องหรือหมดอายุ — ต้อง preview ก่อน
fail_examples: รหัสผ่าน = ... (if context_key matched a Thai security keyword, excluded defensively)
sk_live_abc... (caught earlier by FORBIDDEN_HARDCODE, never reaches this rule)
UI_LITERAL.registry_reference: n/a — validated by shape (whitespace/Thai-script presence) plus the defensive keyword exclusion above, not a registry cross-reference; human-readable text has no central registry to check against in this codebase.
UI_LITERAL.why_not_business_rule_or_secret: Display/log/error text conveys meaning to a human reader, not a machine-consumed threshold, price, or credential — and the security-keyword exclusion is a deliberate extra guard specifically so this category cannot be used to launder a Thai-labeled secret past the (currently English-only) forbidden-pattern keyword list.

TEST_FIXTURE.description: A literal value that only exists inside a test/fixture file — defined for completeness per the owner's allowed-category list, but found ZERO real matches in this phase's critical-path scan (services/gateway/engines/validation/engines/debt/engines/documents/core/executor/app/api/admin/supabase/functions contain no *.test.ts/*.spec.ts/__tests__/__fixtures__ files as of 2026-08-04) — reported honestly rather than fabricating examples.
TEST_FIXTURE.added: HCG Phase 2.7 (2026-08-04), owner-authorized, evidence-based (definition only, 0 real hits this phase)
TEST_FIXTURE.allow_conditions: File path matches /\.(test|spec)\.tsx?$/ or contains /__tests__/ or /__fixtures__/ or /fixtures/, AND the value is not itself a real secret shape (forbidden-pattern check still runs first and wins — a test file with a real-looking credential should still be flagged, since 'it's just a test' doesn't guarantee the value is fake).
TEST_FIXTURE.reject_conditions: File is not under a test/fixture path (falls through to whatever other category applies, or UNKNOWN). Value inside a test file matches a forbidden secret pattern — the file being a test does not grant amnesty for what looks like a real credential.
fail_examples: const apiKey = "sk_live_..." inside *.test.ts — still SECURITY_VIOLATION, test files aren't exempt
TEST_FIXTURE.registry_reference: n/a — validated by file-path shape only.
TEST_FIXTURE.why_not_business_rule_or_secret: Test fixture data exists solely to exercise code paths in isolation from production data/config; it never governs real runtime business behavior and (per the reject condition above) is still subject to the same secret-detection rules as production code.

layer_rules.ui: sends intent only — never originates a constant
layer_rules.route: Request → Validation → Runtime → Response — no constant origination
layer_rules.business_logic: business rules come from Policy or Registry, never inline
layer_rules.hardware_values: must come from Hardware Profile registry, not central logic
